content:
alex: Hey team — hitting a weird streaming issue from our Node/TS app on the Vercel edge. Direct calls to Redwood stream fine, but through our nginx/ALB proxy the SSE/ReadableStream gets buffered and delivered in large blobs (~12-15s). Sometimes we see a 502 right after our auth token rotation. Repro and logs below.

alex: Repro snippet (TypeScript, Node 18):
```ts
const res = await client.responses.stream({
  model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
  input: 'ping',
  stream: true,
});
const reader = (res.body as ReadableStream).getReader();
const decoder = new TextDecoder();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  console.log(decoder.decode(value));
}
```

alex: curl test pointing at our proxy (this is where it stalls):
```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROTATING_KEY" "https://our-api.example.com/v1/responses/stream"
```

maya_support: thanks, can you confirm the SDK version and whether the proxy is doing any header rewrites or token rotation? also which edge runtime (vercel/fastly/cloudflare)?

alex: SDK 0.10.2, Node 18.15, running Vercel Edge for app logic but we route traffic through an nginx ALB (custom domain) that handles API key rotation. The proxy rewrites Authorization header per request.

jordan_runtime: eng-runtime — this smells like proxy buffering. Nginx will buffer small upstream chunks by default and only flush when the buffer is full or idle timeout hits. Two things to check: the `Transfer-Encoding`/`Content-Type` headers coming out of the proxy, and whether the proxy adds any duplicate headers. We also had a bug in SDK <0.11 that could emit duplicate `content-type` header which some proxies treat as non-streaming.

alex: logs from proxy around the 502: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] upstream response chunked 12ms
[2026-03-15T14:02:23Z] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.5, server: our-api.example.com
[2026-03-15T14:02:23Z] 502 Bad Gateway
```

sam_devex: devex here — quick workarounds:
- disable proxy buffering in nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off;` or set response header `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.
- upgrade SDK to `>=0.11.4` (fixes header duplication we saw in older releases).
- for Node edge fetches, ensure `fetch` is used with `{ duplex: 'half' }` if you're using streaming request bodies.

sam_devex: also, when rotating keys, make sure the rotation does not close connections mid-stream. If you swap Authorization for an open connection, proxy behavior varies — prefer rotating only for new connections or use a separate auth-refresh route that returns ephemeral tokens.

alex: tried both: turned off `proxy_buffering` and upgraded SDK to 0.11.4 — streaming is now smooth, chunks arrive ~50ms, and no 502s during key swap. Confirmed direct->redwood and via proxy now match.

jordan_runtime: great. we'll add a short doc note about proxies + SSE and a recommended nginx snippet: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ''; proxy_pass_request_headers on;` and a note about safe key-rotation patterns. Filed ENG-4283 to track adding a dedicated troubleshooting page.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: docs/edge/sse-proxy-guidance -> staging (job: docs-359)

alex: awesome, thanks @maya_support @sam_devex @jordan_runtime :tada:
